goal.en: Hear what a text assumes and implies, not only what it states.
goal.ar: أن تسمع ما يفترضه النص ويُلمح إليه، لا ما يقوله فحسب.

reference.title: A reference for a job applicant
reference.text:
Ms Karim worked in my department for two years. She was always punctual, and her written English is of a good standard. She completed the tasks assigned to her and left on good terms with her colleagues. I am sure she will be an asset to any organisation prepared to invest in her development.

I should add that the role she held was largely administrative, and I am not in a position to comment on her experience of managing budgets, which I understand is central to the post she has applied for.

notice.title: A notice to residents
notice.text: Following feedback from residents, the bin collection will move to Tuesdays from 1 October. We appreciate that this change will not suit everyone. Residents who are unable to present bins on Tuesdays may wish to make arrangements with a neighbour. The council is unable to provide individual collections.

text.en: In references and reviews, what is left out speaks louder than what is said. Praising someone for punctuality suggests there was nothing stronger to praise.
text.ar: في خطابات التزكية والمراجعات يتكلم المسكوت عنه أعلى من المذكور. فالثناء على الالتزام بالمواعيد يوحي بأنه لم يكن هناك ما هو أقوى للثناء عليه.

head: Written
Understood as
rows: There is little else to say.
An asset to any organisation prepared to invest in her development.
I am not in a position to comment on X.
There is no evidence she can do X.

text.en: Ask of any recommendation: what would a genuinely enthusiastic version say that this one does not?
text.ar: اسأل عن أي تزكية: ماذا كانت ستقول النسخة المتحمسة حقاً مما لم تقله هذه؟

title.en: What a sentence takes for granted

text.en: Some words smuggle in an assumption that survives even when the sentence is denied. “He has stopped missing deadlines” assumes he used to miss them — and so does “He hasn't stopped missing deadlines.”
text.ar: بعض الكلمات تُهرّب افتراضاً يبقى قائماً حتى لو نُفيت الجملة. فجملة He has stopped missing deadlines تفترض أنه كان يفوّتها، وكذلك نفيها.

head: Trigger
It assumes
rows: it happened at least once already
this case is surprising or extreme
others were expected but did not apply

text.en: Presupposition is how a loaded question works. “Have you fixed the errors in your report?” assumes there are errors — answering yes or no accepts that.
text.ar: على هذا المبدأ يقوم السؤال المُلغَّم. فسؤال «هل صحّحت الأخطاء في تقريرك؟» يفترض وجود أخطاء، والإجابة بنعم أو لا تُقرّ بها.

head: Written
Means
rows: we had complaints, or we had already decided
We appreciate that this will not suit everyone
we know you will object, and we are proceeding
Residents may wish to make arrangements
the council will not, and there is no appeal

text.en: “Unable to” usually means unwilling; a real inability is normally explained. Notice which one you are being offered.
text.ar: عبارة unable to تعني غالباً «غير راغب»، إذ العجز الحقيقي يُفسَّر عادةً. فانتبه أيّهما يُعرض عليك.

text.en: This is not dishonesty so much as convention. Reading it accurately saves you from arguing with a wall — or from missing a real offer.
text.ar: هذا عرف أكثر منه خداعاً. وقراءته بدقة تجنّبك مجادلة الجدار، أو تفويت عرضٍ حقيقي.

options: Lukewarm: it praises only basic reliability.
Strong: it recommends her without reservation.
Hostile: it accuses her of poor performance.
Neutral: it gives only dates and job titles.

explanation.en: Punctuality, completing assigned tasks and leaving on good terms are the minimum, not a recommendation.
explanation.ar: الالتزام بالمواعيد وإنجاز المهام المكلّف بها وحسن المغادرة هي الحد الأدنى، لا تزكية.

prompt.en: What does “an asset to any organisation prepared to invest in her development” imply?

options: She will need significant training first.
She is ready for a senior role immediately.
She has already been fully trained by the writer.
She invests her own money in her training.

explanation.en: The condition attached to the praise is the message: the praise applies only if you train her.
explanation.ar: الشرط الملحق بالمدح هو الرسالة: المدح لا يصحّ إلا إذا تولّيت تدريبها.

prompt.en: Why does the second paragraph mention budgets?
prompt.ar: لماذا ذُكرت الميزانيات في الفقرة الثانية؟

options: To signal she has no track record in the job's core duty.
To confirm she managed large budgets successfully.
To praise her financial skills indirectly.
To explain why she left the department.

explanation.en: Naming the skill and declining to comment is a warning delivered without a single negative word.
explanation.ar: ذكر المهارة مع الامتناع عن التعليق تحذيرٌ بلا كلمة سلبية واحدة.

prompt.en: Which sentence belongs in a genuinely strong reference?
prompt.ar: أي جملة تنتمي إلى تزكية قوية فعلاً؟

options: She rebuilt our reporting process and trained the team herself.
She was always punctual and completed the tasks assigned.
She left on good terms with everyone in the department.
She has a good standard of written and spoken English.

explanation.en: Specific achievement beyond the job description is what a real recommendation contains.
explanation.ar: الإنجاز المحدد الذي يتجاوز وصف الوظيفة هو ما تحتويه التزكية الحقيقية.

prompt.en: “Has the team stopped missing deadlines?” What does the question assume?

options: The team was missing deadlines before.
The team has never missed a deadline.
The team will miss deadlines in future.
The team has no deadlines to meet.

explanation.en: “Stop” presupposes the action was happening — and the assumption survives a “no”.
explanation.ar: فعل stop يفترض أن الأمر كان يحدث، والافتراض يبقى حتى مع الإجابة بـ«لا».

prompt.en: “Even the finance team approved it.” What does “even” signal?
prompt.ar: ماذا تشير إليه كلمة even هنا؟

options: Their approval was the least expected.
They approved it before anyone else did.
They were the only team to approve it.
They approved it without reading it.

explanation.en: “Even” marks the case as surprising, which tells you what the writer expected.
explanation.ar: even تصف الحالة بأنها مفاجئة، وهذا يكشف ما كان يتوقعه الكاتب.

prompt.en: “We have again postponed the launch.” What is assumed?

options: The launch has been postponed before.
The launch will definitely happen soon.
This is the first delay to the launch.
The launch was cancelled permanently.

explanation.en: “Again” presupposes at least one earlier occurrence — a small word carrying a history.
explanation.ar: كلمة again تفترض وقوعاً سابقاً واحداً على الأقل، وهي كلمة صغيرة تحمل تاريخاً.

prompt.en: Why is “Have you fixed the errors in your report?” a difficult question to answer?
prompt.ar: لماذا يصعب الرد على هذا السؤال؟

options: Yes and no both accept that there are errors.
It contains a grammatical mistake of its own.
It can only be answered by the report's author.
It uses a tense that has no clear meaning.

explanation.en: The presupposition sits outside the yes/no choice, so answering at all concedes it.
explanation.ar: الافتراض خارج خيار نعم/لا، فمجرد الإجابة إقرارٌ به.

prompt.en: Match the word with what it assumes.

explanation.en: These words carry assumptions that a reader accepts without noticing.
explanation.ar: هذه الكلمات تحمل افتراضات يقبلها القارئ دون أن ينتبه.

prompt.en: What does “Following feedback from residents” most likely mean here?
prompt.ar: ماذا تعني عبارة Following feedback from residents هنا على الأرجح؟

options: The council is presenting its decision as responsive.
Residents voted directly on the new collection day.
Every resident asked for a Tuesday collection.
The change was requested by the bin contractors.

explanation.en: The phrase frames a decision as a response, without saying what the feedback actually asked for.
explanation.ar: تُصوّر العبارة القرار استجابةً، دون أن تذكر ما طلبته تلك الملاحظات فعلاً.

prompt.en: What is the practical message of the last two sentences?

options: If Tuesday does not work for you, solve it yourself.
The council will arrange collections on request.
Residents may choose their own collection day.
The change will be reversed if people object.

explanation.en: “May wish to make arrangements with a neighbour” plus “unable to provide individual collections” closes the door politely.
explanation.ar: عبارتا «قد ترغب في الترتيب مع جار» و«غير قادر على توفير جمع فردي» تغلقان الباب بلطف.

prompt.en: An organisation writes “we are unable to offer a refund”. What is usually true?
prompt.ar: كتبت مؤسسة we are unable to offer a refund. ما الصحيح غالباً؟

options: It is a policy choice presented as an impossibility.
A law prevents them from issuing any refund.
Their payment system has broken down.
They will refund you if you ask twice.

explanation.en: Genuine inability is normally explained; “unable to” without a reason is usually “will not”.
explanation.ar: العجز الحقيقي يُفسَّر عادةً، وunable to بلا سبب تعني غالباً «لن نفعل».

prompt.en: You must refuse a customer's request but keep the relationship. Which is best?
prompt.ar: عليك رفض طلب عميل مع الحفاظ على العلاقة. ما الأفضل؟

options: We can't refund this order, but I can offer a credit for your next one.
We are unable to assist you with this matter at the present time.
Unfortunately our policy does not permit us to do what you ask.
This is not something that we would ever be able to consider.

explanation.en: A clear refusal with a real alternative respects the reader; the others hide behind institutional phrasing.
explanation.ar: الرفض الواضح مع بديل حقيقي يحترم المتلقي، أما البقية فتختبئ خلف صيغ مؤسسية.

prompt.en: A reviewer writes: “The book is competently organised.” What is implied?
prompt.ar: كتب ناقد: The book is competently organised. ما المعنى الضمني؟

options: The organisation is adequate and nothing more.
The book is outstanding in every respect.
The book is disorganised and hard to follow.
The reviewer did not finish reading it.

explanation.en: “Competently” praises the floor, not the ceiling — faint praise is a judgement in disguise.
explanation.ar: كلمة competently تمدح الحد الأدنى لا الأعلى، والمدح الفاتر حكمٌ متنكّر.

prompt.en: “I was surprised that the report was finished on time.” What is assumed?

options: The report was in fact finished on time.
The report was submitted several days late.
The speaker wrote the report themselves.
Nobody expected the report to be written.

explanation.en: “Surprised that” presupposes the fact is true; the surprise is about expectation, not fact.
explanation.ar: عبارة surprised that تفترض صحة الواقعة، والدهشة تتعلق بالتوقع لا بالحقيقة.
